look_here_first: Find an opposite SIMPLE leaf with very deep, sharp, angular/V-shaped sinuses and a conspicuously pale to silvery lower face. Check multiple mature leaves, not a single atypical blade; confirm opposite twig nodes and paired samaras when present.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Fast-growing deciduous tree, often associated with moist bottomlands; site alone does not prove ID.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, simple, palmately 3–5-lobed; lobes often long and sharply pointed, separated by conspicuously deep sinuses. Lower surface silvery or whitish; sparse hairs may also occur.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Small early-season flowers may open before leaves; seasonal timing is supportive, not decisive.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Paired winged samaras, often ripening in spring; inspect wing shape with scale.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite SIMPLE leaf with very deep V-shaped sinuses

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: silvery/pale abaxial surface; some hairs possible

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: long pointed lobes, check several mature leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: paired winged samaras, frequently early in season
